en: Water expands when it freezes, so leaving a sealed glass bottle of water in the freezer can cause the glass to shatter.
Mixing bleach and white vinegar produces toxic chlorine gas, so you must never combine these two common household cleaning liquids.
Chewing food thoroughly is a physical change that increases the food's surface area, making it much easier for your stomach to digest.
Aerosol spray cans contain gases under high pressure, so leaving them in a hot car can cause the metal can to explode.
Drinking seawater is dangerous because its high salt concentration draws water out of your body's cells, causing severe dehydration.
Rubber is an electrical insulator, which is why electricians wear thick rubber gloves to protect their hands from dangerous electric shocks.
Squeezing lemon juice on a sliced apple prevents browning because the citric acid slows the chemical reaction between the fruit and oxygen.
Filtering muddy water through a clean cloth removes solid dirt, but you must still boil the water to kill microscopic germs before drinking.
Carbon dioxide gas is heavier than air, which is why carbon dioxide fire extinguishers work by sinking over flames to block oxygen.
Baking soda neutralizes acidic odors in refrigerators because it is a base that chemically reacts with and neutralizes acidic smell molecules.
Mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature that releases toxic vapors, so you must never touch it if an old thermometer breaks.
Dissolving salt in water increases the liquid's boiling point, which is why adding salt makes pasta water boil at a slightly higher temperature.
